what: One entry per refusal the server throws that a skill reference instructs a caller into. The check is scripts/check-refusal-parity.mjs; the gate over it is mcp-server/test-refusal-parity.mjs (GATE RP1, design/survey-depth/spec.md §8.7).
how_to_read: server.phrase is the server's own words, compared against the named file's source and against the messages that file composes — a sentence wrapped across a concatenation is still one sentence. A reference may carry its own phrase when the prose needs fewer words, and that phrase must be part of the server's sentence: a reference may quote less than the server says, never something else. refuses names advertised tools the server states the refusal at — thrown from the handler, through whatever it calls, or documented in the tool's own definition — and every name is checked against those call sites. instructs names advertised tools a reference calling them must warn about and which do not refuse themselves; start_session is the repair for the active-session requirement, not a tool that throws it. Their union is what the reference-side scan searches the skill for. refuses must be true of every tool it names; it is not required to name every tool, which is why the candidate set is derived from the server's messages rather than from this file.
limits: String identity over a hand-maintained list. It catches a reference edited out of agreement with the server; it cannot tell whether either side is right. A refusal nobody registers drifts freely — which is why the candidate set is derived from the server's own messages rather than from this file (spec.md §6.2, §8.7).
